Without the fiddling it does 64c on max usage. Also not to mention the fan is pointing upwards into the shittiest part of the case, there is literally 2 sata cables like 3mm away from the fan and the fan has about 6cm of breathing space above it, and that's being ambitious because that space is also filled with a bunch of cables. comments.text:
It's not an "inferior" cooler, it's a DIFFERENT category of cooler.  The rear-exhausting blower style is a fundamentally different application than the 3rd-party axial-fan coolers.  The "superior" performance of the axial-fan coolers, only works in a big open case with lots of airflow.  Some folks need the option of the Nvidia reference/Founder's style cooler, 'cause nothing else works in a cramped compact case, like some Mini-ITX builds, etc.  (Or an air-cooled SLI setup with no space between cards.) 

Within the constraints of the latter applications, the Nvidia reference/Founder's vapor-chamber cooler IS amazing.  You just can't make apples & oranges comparisons to the other category.  A rear-exhaust cooler WILL work in an open-flow case, but an axial-fan cooler WON'T work in any airflow-starved setup.  So when Nvidia chooses the one standard configuration for their baseline model, they obviously choose the one that DOES work in all applications.  It's a little less efficient in some typical scenarios, but that's better than not working AT ALL the other half of the time.
